name: NA61/SHINE
notes: Placed in EHN1 (the NA61/SHINE Beams page says the beam is transported to Experimental Hall North 1); the site record is the existing site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1, which carries a coarse campus point (see its notes). Refining it with the MapCERN building 887 (EHN1) centroid (46.26122, 6.05717) is left for the integrator.
Status shutdown reflects the SPS stop for Long Shutdown 3 on 2026-08-31 (restart planned from 2028 onwards).
The first run of 2007 is the earliest documented data; the JINST paper states first physics data with hadron beams in 2009 and with ion beams in 2011 (the 2007 sample was a pilot run).

physics_goals.value: Study the onset of deconfinement and search for the critical point of strongly interacting matter; measure hadron production for neutrino and cosmic-ray physics

summary.plain: NA61/SHINE studies what happens when protons and nuclei collide with fixed targets at CERN's SPS. It scans collision energy and system size to look for the onset of quark-gluon plasma formation and a critical point, and measures hadron production needed for neutrino and cosmic-ray experiments.
summary.technical: SPS Heavy Ion and Neutrino Experiment (NA61) on the H2 beam line in the North Area: large-acceptance spectrometer with four time projection chambers (two Vertex TPCs in superconducting magnets, up to 9 Tm), ToF walls and the PSD calorimeter, inherited largely from NA49; collision energy / system size scan with p, Be, Ar and Xe beams, p+p and hadron-nucleus data for T2K/NuMI neutrino fluxes and cosmic-ray air showers; approved 2007, running 2007-2026 until LS3.
